tagline: Lunar landers (NASA CLPS), lunar data relay (NASA Near Space Network) and, since buying Lanteris (formerly Maxar Space Systems), satellites for commercial, civil and national-security customers.

notes: The jump from Q1 2026 is mostly the Lanteris acquisition (closed Jan 13, 2026): $800M before adjustments, paid as ~$403M cash plus 22,991,028 Class A shares issued at $12.34.

Q2 bookings were $920M (about 4.5x book-to-bill): three commercial GEO satellites (a program worth more than $600M), a sixth NASA CLPS mission (CS-8), and expanded IM-5, IM-6 and NSN values. Another ~$300M was booked in Q3 through Aug 13, including 18 AMDT3 'Golden Dome' satellites for L3Harris.
Management expects 25–30% of the Q2 backlog to turn into 2026 revenue and 35–40% in 2027. National-security revenue rose from 3% to 30% of the total year over year.
The company closed the Goonhilly Earth Station (UK) and COMSAT acquisitions in August 2026 to build out its space-to-ground data network.
Q2 missed estimates: adjusted EPS −$0.29 vs −$0.09 expected, and revenue $206.2M vs about $212M expected.
Insiders sold 12.2M shares (~$158.6M) over the three months to late September, per MarketBeat's Form 4 tally. Institutions hold ~78% and insiders ~4% of shares (StockAnalysis).

calls.text: Consensus Strong Buy across 9 analysts (8 Strong Buy, 1 Sell); average target $29.50, range $13–$43

catalysts.event: NASA CLPS 2.0 award, delayed from October: a multi-award follow-on to CLPS that the company puts at about $10B
Q3 2026 earnings: backlog, the $900M–$1.0B guide and the path to positive adjusted EBITDA
IM-3 (CLPS CP-11) launches on a Falcon 9 to Reiner Gamma with 12 payloads and deploys the Altus-1 lunar relay satellite. It slipped from 2026.
NASA Lunar Terrain Vehicle task orders: a ~$4.5B, ~10-year award shared by 3 vendors, with only small initial orders in May 2026. IM is building a heavier Nova-C variant to deliver an LTV.
IM-4 lunar mission (CLPS), which management says is on track
Altus-2 to Altus-5 launch together on a dedicated flight, ahead of the original schedule, for full Near Space Network lunar relay coverage
NASA Near Space Network Services contract (lunar relay, navigation): firm-fixed-price IDIQ, maximum potential value $4.82B

bull.text: Backlog rose more than 8x in six months to $1.76B, about 2x the 2026 revenue guide, and Q2 book-to-bill was ~4.5x
Lanteris turns a lumpy lunar-lander business into a satellite prime with commercial GEO, civil and national-security customers. Defense was 30% of Q2 revenue.
NASA work spans three lines: a sixth CLPS mission (CS-8), a Near Space Network contract worth up to $4.82B, and a position for LTV and CLPS 2.0
Analysts' $29.50 average target is about 2x the price, and the forward P/S has fallen to ~3x after the 68% drop from the May peak

bear.text: Losses continue: TTM net loss −$131.2M, FCF −$187.8M, and Q2 adjusted EPS missed by $0.20
Heavy dilution: the share count is up 44.6% YoY from the acquisition stock and $291M of at-the-market sales
Mission and schedule risk: IM-1 and IM-2 both ended on their sides, IM-3 slipped to 2027, and fixed-price lunar programs carry cost overrun risk
Timing of NASA awards: CLPS 2.0 was pushed to Nov 7 and LTV task orders are slow. Insiders sold ~$158.6M in three months, and short interest is 27.6% of float.

runContext.title: The 2026 round trip
runContext.summary: LUNR closed at a 52-week low of $8.05 on Nov 20, 2025, two weeks after the Lanteris deal was announced. It peaked at $45.70 on May 28, 2026 and has since fallen 68% to $14.41 (Oct 7), even as backlog hit a record.
signals: Q2 missed on EPS and revenue (Aug 13), and costs tripled with the Lanteris integration.
The share count rose 44.6% YoY from the acquisition stock and at-the-market sales at ~$26.81.
IM-3 slipped from 2026 to Q1 2027, and NASA pushed the CLPS 2.0 award to Nov 7.
Space stocks sold off on SpaceX's reported $40B debt plan; insiders sold ~$158.6M in three months.
runContext.caveat: Backlog and analysts' targets point the other way: $1.76B in backlog and a $29.50 average target. Risk It scores momentum separately, and LUNR's 1-yr relative strength is only modest.

news.title: IM-3 'Trinity' now targeted for Q1 2027
news.summary: NASA says the 'first part of 2027' (it had said 2026 in May), and the CEO says Q1 2027. The mission flies to Reiner Gamma with Lunar Vertex and ESA and KASI payloads.

news.title: LUNR down ~25% in 30 days

listContext.method: Risk It is a maximum-growth screen that accepts much higher risk. We start from every US-listed stock in the StockAnalysis / S&P Global screener and keep those with a market cap over $300M, at least $10M a day of average trading volume, TTM revenue of $50M or more, coverage from 5+ analysts with a price target, and growth that is current and expected to continue (latest-quarter revenue up 15%+ YoY and consensus revenue growth of 15%+ this fiscal year and 10%+ next). Mortgage REITs, SPACs and anything already in Growth Picks are excluded. Each stock is scored 0–100: TTM revenue growth up to 40

gradeNote: Growth is graded on revenue alone (no 3-year EPS forecast) and Value on EV/sales alone (no forward P/E or PEG while it loses money), hence the * marks. Most of the +117% TTM revenue growth comes from the Lanteris acquisition (closed Jan 13, 2026) rather than organic growth.
